g.text: What separates stabilised peptides from unstabilised ones, with the N-terminal residue held fixed

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 6.6px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: middle; fill: #6b6b6b

g.text: A–C composition of positions 3–24, the part the motif does not fix · D–E the same comparison inside matched baseline-PSI bands, which rules out the stability ceiling as the explanation

text.style: font-size: 5.8px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #6b6b6b

g.text: Stabilised = ΔPSI ≥ 1.0 with baseline PSI ≤ 4.0 (Met-Pro: in any of ZYG11B KO, ZER1 KO, double KO; Met-Gly: double KO). Not stabilised = ΔPSI < 0.5 everywhere measured. Boxes are median and quartiles, whiskers 1.5 IQR, every peptide drawn. Mann-Whitney throughout.

text.style: font-size: 5.8px; font-family: 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #6b6b6b

g.text: Among unstabilised Met-Pro peptides acidic content rises WITH baseline stability (Spearman r = +0.22, p = 8e-06), so the ceiling cannot manufacture panels A and D — it works against them. The same composition separates Met-Gly substrates more strongly than Met-Pro ones, so this is not proline-specific.
